E.name: Stationary Bilateral Ankle Pogo
E.job: Main repeated ankle-spring practice. Hands on hips; make small two-foot bounces in place, with soft knees and ankles moving freely. Record the quality marker. End the set if rhythm/position deteriorates; use lower amplitude instead of chasing height.
E.source_dose: **2 × 8 hops**, bodyweight; **60 s after each set**

E.name: Single-Leg Pogo in Place
E.job: Apply spring-like ankle force while one leg supports the pelvis. Hands on hips; stay over the foot and finish balanced. Reduce amplitude for drift; if needed, use light fingertip support on a stable bench **instead of** unsupported execution, with the same dose. Do not change this to alternating jogging.
E.source_dose: **1 × 4 hops per leg**; **90 s between legs and after the second leg**

E.name: Single-Leg Forward Hop to Stick
E.job: Quick single-leg push followed by controlled forward weight acceptance. Take off and land on the **same leg** over a short, self-selected distance, no more than one of the athlete's foot lengths today. Hold 2 s, then walk back and reset. Use a shorter distance instead of a farther unstable landing; stop for repeated extra balance steps.
E.source_dose: **1 × 3 per leg**; **12–15 s between reps**, **90 s between legs and afterward**

E.name: Squat Jump — paused, hands on hips
E.job: Express hip/knee extension quickly from stillness, complementing the ankle-dominant anchor. Hold a comfortable quarter-to-half squat for 2 s, jump vertically without another dip, then absorb and hold the two-foot landing for 2 s. Lower jump height for a hard landing; repeated re-dipping ends the task.

E.name: Split-Squat Jump to Stick — no leg switch
E.job: Produce quick force from an asymmetric stance while keeping the pelvis facing forward. From a comfortable floor split stance, dip shallowly, jump a small height and land in the **same stance**, holding 2 s. Both feet participate: this is not a single-leg landing. Use a shallower dip/lower flight instead of switching legs or losing alignment.
E.source_dose: **1 × 3 per lead leg**; **12–15 s between reps**, **90 s between sides and afterward**

E.name: Two-hand Kettlebell Swing
E.job: Rapid hip extension against an external load, with **no additional jump landing**. Hinge, snap hips tall and let the bell float to no higher than chest height; feet stay planted. Park under control after rep five. Reduce the bell load for arm lifting, back extension or slowing; stop if the hinge cannot stay controlled.
E.source_dose: **2 × 5 swings**; light-to-moderate bell selected for crisp speed; **90 s after each set**

S.name: Short-Foot Drill
S.job: Strengthen active arch control for a stable contact platform. Stand on both feet; gently draw the target forefoot toward its heel without curling toes or raising the heel. Only one foot is targeted at a time. Use seated execution **instead of** standing if toe gripping or cramping appears.

S.name: Side-lying Hip Abduction
S.job: Light hip-abductor strengthening for pelvic support in single-leg stance. Bottom knee bent, top leg straight and slightly behind the trunk; raise only while the pelvis stays stacked. Reduce the range for rolling/hiking; no band or burnout today.

P.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides
P.cue: Floor split stance, front foot planted, pelvis square; lower 2 s and rise firmly for 1 s. Reduce load/range for collapse or balance loss. Use one DB with stable hand support instead of two unsupported DBs if needed; counts stay the same.

P.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
P.cue: Soft knees, hips back, DBs close; lower 3 s and rise in 1 s. Stop the descent before back rounding; reduce load/range if the hinge becomes spinal movement.
P.job: Loaded hip extension and hamstring force through the stance hinge.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Knee-flexed plantarflexor force for stance support.

P.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — supported single leg
P.cue: Work from floor, near-straight soft knee, one DB and stable hand support. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load or use bodyweight for lost range; use 1 × 8 bilateral instead of per-leg work if even unilateral bodyweight is too demanding, with 1 × 4 bilateral preparation.
P.job: Straight-knee plantarflexor force complementing knee-flexed work.

P.name: Glute Bridge Walkout
P.cue: Keep a floor bridge while four small alternating heel steps go out and four return; eight steps at about 1 s each = one full cycle. Choose reach so four cycles are challenging with 2–3 whole cycles available. Shorten reach for pelvic sag or cramping; do not add steps or cycles.
P.job: Hamstring force as knee angle changes with the pelvis supported.

P.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
P.cue: Secure loop band around both forefeet; nonworking leg straight with heel grounded. Flex working hip/knee toward thigh-vertical in 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without arching or moving the anchor heel. Reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt. If a secure loop is unavailable, use seated DB hip flexion instead with hands securing the DB above the knee: same dose/rest, small controlled thigh lift; preparation unloaded.
P.job: Resisted swing-leg recovery under a quiet pelvis.
